document_check.note: Mancioppi G, Fiorini L, Rovini E, Cavallo F. 'The use of Motor and Cognitive Dual-Task quantitative assessment on subjects with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review', Mechanisms of Ageing and Development 193 (2021) 111393. It is a systematic review of 38 studies. The cited statement that protocols remain unstandardised matches the abstract and the conclusion.

cited_result: The review's conclusion that motor and cognitive dual-task (MCDT) protocols, instruments and outcome measures are heterogeneous and need standardising and harmonising (p. 1 abstract; p. 17 conclusion).
tool_reason: The cited result is a conclusion drawn from a systematic review of 38 primary studies, so ROBIS applies.

domains.rationale: No protocol or pre-specified criteria are reported. One exclusion criterion is subjective ('did not appear suitable'). Studies were excluded for being non-English or not full access, which is a restriction by source that can bias the evidence base.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: Searched the methods (pp. 2-3) for 'protocol', 'registration', 'PROSPERO' and 'pre-defined': no protocol or registration is mentioned; only 'According to the PRISMA statement Moher et al. (2015), an additional manual search was performed'.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: (1) they did not encompass any type of technological methods for kinematics evaluation (electronic walkways, wearable sensors, optical systems, and/or personal devices); (2) they did not manage MCI subjects; (3) they did not refer to MCDT approach

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: (4) they did not appear suitable for this review after regarding of title and abstract; or (5) they were not full access.

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: In addition, (6) if multiple articles written by same authors had similar content, more recent articles have been selected.

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: (2) they were not written in the English language; (3) were from years prior to 2010. ... or (5) they were not full access.

domains.domain: Domain 2: Identification and selection of studies
domains.rationale: The review searched three databases and did a manual citation search, and screening was done independently. However, language, publication-format and full-access restrictions were applied and no grey literature was searched. The reported search window is also inconsistent: May 2019 to May 2020 in the methods, but January 2010 to May 2020 elsewhere.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: An electronic database search was performed for the period from May 2019 until May 2020 using the U.S. National Library of Medicine (PubMed®), Web of Science (ISI®), and Scopus® databases

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: an additional manual search was performed (e.g., through citations of articles included in this review).

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: (”swing time” OR ”stance time” OR cadence OR stride OR MCDT OR ”motor-cognitive dual task” OR walking OR gait) AND (CIND OR ... OR MCI OR ”Mild Cognitive Impairment”). The terms research was performed regarding titles and/or abstracts.

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: items were excluded if: (1) they were an abstract, a letter, a review article, or a chapter from a book; (2) they were not written in the English language

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: Each author independently screened the articles ... Disagreements on the inclusion/exclusion and classification of the articles were solved through meetings and discussion.

domains.domain: Domain 3: Data collection and study appraisal
domains.rationale: Study characteristics are tabulated in detail. However, nothing is said about duplicate extraction, and no risk-of-bias or quality appraisal of the included studies was done: the text contains no 'quality', 'bias' or 'appraisal' assessment.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: Data were abstracted from each selected articles, as reported in Tables 1–3. (Searched for duplicate or independent extraction: none reported.)

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: For each article information about the study characteristics (MCI diagnostic criteria, sample size, demographic data, and sample composition) were reported.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Lastly, a list of motor parameters extracted and analyzed have been included.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: Data were abstracted from each selected articles, as reported in Tables 1–3. (The data abstraction section lists characteristics, criteria, batteries, protocols and parameters only; searched the whole text for 'quality', 'bias', 'risk of', 'apprais': no appraisal.)

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: No risk-of-bias assessment was carried out (searched 'quality', 'bias', 'apprais' throughout the document).

domains.rationale: The synthesis is narrative and covers all 38 studies. Heterogeneity of protocols is described, and that description is the cited result. There were no sensitivity analyses, no protocol against which to check the analyses, and primary-study biases were not addressed apart from a remark on small samples.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: All 38 papers are illustrated in detail in Tables 1–3.

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: No protocol or pre-specified analysis plan reported (searched 'protocol', 'pre-specified', 'registration').

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: Finally, the selected articles, fully evaluated and included, were classified into three groups

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Since the breadth of tools that are used to measure motor parameters during MCDT are vast, as are the range of protocols for data collection and the outcome measures that are extracted, there is an urgent need to standardize and harmonize approaches.

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: No sensitivity or robustness analysis reported (searched 'sensitivity', 'robust', 'funnel').

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: Either concerning a 10-years time span, or narrowing the search on the last 2 years, a larger part of articles took into account samples with small sizes.

domains.domain: Phase 3: Risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The conclusions do not address the concerns found in domains 1 to 4: there is no limitations section and no caveat about unappraised primary studies. The aims speak of selecting the 'most valuable' and 'most outstanding' works.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
signalling.quote: In conclusion, quantitative and objective MCDT data might furnish landmarks to clinicians, enriching the tools they could use and might supply aid for: disease stratification, risk prediction, tracking disease progression, and decision making for intervention optimization and maximizing therapeutic response.

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: Analyzing all the papers, it is possible identifying and grouping the barriers and opportunities within this research topic.

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: Thus, this review aim at collecting and summarizing the most outstanding works in the field of quantitative motor assessment by the use of MCDT on MCI subjects.

overall_rationale: All four ROBIS phase 2 domains raise high concern. There is no protocol, the criteria are ambiguous, and English-only and full-access restrictions were applied. Extraction was single or unreported, there was no appraisal of primary studies, and the synthesis is narrative with no robustness checks. The phase 3 interpretation does not acknowledge these concerns.
